meld20.title: Laboratory MELD 3.0
meld20.context: Model estimate; transplantation and exceptions censored
meld20.caution: A model illustration, not HCC cancer survival or the risk associated with exception MELD 20. Do not substitute older MELD mortality tables.
definitions: MELD 3.0 uses bilirubin, INR, creatinine, sodium, albumin and sex. Laboratory urgency and tumor exception priority are different.
meld20.uncertainty: A confidence interval for this worked model estimate was not supplied.

child.title: Child-Pugh and HCC survival
child.caution: Historical treated cohort; these are not universal cirrhosis life-expectancy estimates. Groups were not randomized.
definitions: Child-Pugh: A = 5–6, B = 7–9, C = 10–15 points. The score combines bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites and encephalopathy.
child.uncertainty: 95% CI: A 12.8–14.7 months; B 4.6–6.3 months. The n shown is the full intention-to-treat registry.

pvtt.title: Portal-vein tumor invasion: Vp1–4
pvtt.population: IMbrave150; systemic-treatment-naive, unresectable HCC; Child-Pugh A
pvtt.caution: Exploratory prognostic comparison; invasion groups were not randomized. “Without Vp4” includes Vp1–3; it does not mean no vascular invasion.
definitions: Vp1: tumor thrombus distal to second-order portal branches, without involving them.
Vp2: second-order portal branch.
Vp3: first-order right or left portal branch.
Vp4: main portal trunk and/or a branch opposite the primarily involved lobe.
These categories describe tumor thrombus, not bland thrombosis.
pvtt.uncertainty: 95% CI: Vp4 6.0–13.9 months; without Vp4 18.0–24.6 months. The without-Vp4 group may include bile-duct invasion or ≥50% liver involvement.

afp-response.title: AFP response before transplant
afp-response.population: Deceased-donor HCC recipients with AFP >1,000 while waitlisted; UNOS 2005–2015
afp-response.caution: Selected transplant recipients; association does not establish a treatment effect. The 500–1,000 group is not shown; these rows are not current allocation rules.
afp-response.uncertainty: Last AFP within 90 days before LT. The 500–1,000 group (n=17) is not displayed. 101–499 versus ≤100 was not significant (P=0.09); treatment and waiting-time differences confound comparisons.

ras-os.title: RAS mutation and resection outcomes
ras-os.population: Resected CRLM after one bevacizumab-containing preoperative regimen; no anti-EGFR
ras-os.caution: RAS mutations occurred in 18% of this selected surgical cohort, not 18% of all metastatic CRC. Prognostic association; a mutation alone is not a resection prohibition.
definitions: RAS includes KRAS and NRAS; wild-type means no tested pathogenic mutation was identified.
ras-os.uncertainty: Selected tissue cohort: tumors with <5% viable cells and 90-day deaths excluded; 95/288 eligible lacked tissue. Hotspot RAS assay, not extended sequencing. Intervals for these survival estimates are not reported in the article.

braf-os.title: BRAF status and resection outcomes
braf-os.caution: BRAF-mutated tumors: 43/849 (5.1%). The median pools BRAF variants; the adverse adjusted association was driven by V600E. Non-V600E cases were few.
definitions: BRAF V600E and non-V600E mutations should be reported separately. This cohort does not establish transplant candidacy.
braf-os.uncertainty: Confidence intervals for the displayed medians were not stated in the cited Discussion. V600E adjusted OS HR 2.76 (95% CI 1.74–4.37).

sidedness.title: Colon primary: left versus right
sidedness.caution: Observational surgical cohort; does not measure the benefit of surgery or predict post-transplant survival.
definitions: COLOMIC defines right-sided as cecum through the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon; left-sided is distal to that point, including the rectum.
sidedness.uncertainty: Log-rank P=0.043; confidence intervals not reported. Of 884 patients, 13 bilateral and 12 unknown primaries were outside these two strata. Methods describe follow-up following hepatectomy; an explicit OS time-zero sentence was not identified.

transmet.title: CRLM: transplant plus chemotherapy
transmet.population: TransMet; selected, permanently unresectable, liver-only, chemotherapy-responsive, BRAF-nonmutated CRLM
transmet.caution: Results require trial-like selection and allocation access; they do not apply to active extrahepatic disease.
definitions: Intention to treat includes all randomized patients, whether or not they received the assigned transplant.

msi.title: MSI-H / dMMR: treatment outcomes
msi.caution: Both arms have MSI-H/dMMR disease. This is not mutant-versus-wild-type prognosis; 62% effective crossover to PD-(L)1 therapy complicates interpretation.
definitions: MSI-H = high microsatellite instability; dMMR = deficient mismatch repair.
msi.uncertainty: OS HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.53–0.99), long-term exploratory follow-up; 5-year percentage CIs not in abstract.

icca-ngs.title: iCCA: molecular alteration frequency
icca-ngs.population: MSK prospective tissue sequencing; intrahepatic subgroup
icca-ngs.caution: Referral-cohort frequencies vary by assay and population. Table counts are used. Targetable alterations do not by themselves establish a survival advantage.
definitions: FGFR2 therapy requires a qualifying fusion/rearrangement, not just any FGFR2 alteration.
icca-ngs.uncertainty: Descriptive counts; confidence intervals not reported. The paper’s abstract uses different percentages; this card follows Table 3.

idh1.title: IDH1-mutated CCA: ClarIDHy
idh1.caution: Unadjusted OS difference was not statistically significant; 43 placebo patients crossed over. This compares therapies within IDH1-mutated disease, not mutation versus wild-type.
idh1.uncertainty: 95% CI: 7.8–12.4 versus 4.8–11.1 months; HR 0.79 (0.56–1.12). Corrected crossover-adjusted HR CI is 0.25–1.24 with bootstrapping; do not use the older narrow CI as definitive.

fgfr2.title: FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement: response
fgfr2.caution: Single-arm response, not cure or a randomized survival advantage. Other FGFR alterations were not this study’s selection marker.
fgfr2.uncertainty: 95% CI 32–52%. Median duration of response 9.7 months.

icca-multiple.title: iCCA: multifocal tumor burden
icca-multiple.population: Multifocal iCCA within a 1,502-patient international resection cohort
icca-multiple.caution: Retrospective, data-derived cutoff; not a validated transplant rule. Location alone does not establish whether lesions are clonally related.
definitions: Multifocal = more than one tumor. In this study, satellites were in the same Couinaud segment; intrahepatic metastases were in different segments. These are study-specific geographic definitions.
TBS = √[(largest diameter in cm)² + (tumor number)²]. Record lesion count, size, segments and lobes rather than only “multifocal.”
icca-multiple.uncertainty: Median OS: 33.1 months (95% CI 24.6–54.0) versus 17.2 (14.8–20.5). Three-year percentage CIs not stated in Results.

icca-lt.title: iCCA: historical transplant selection
icca-lt.population: iCCA identified on explant after transplant for HCC or decompensated cirrhosis
icca-lt.caution: Small ≤2 cm subgroup. Explant-defined retrospective groups; these results do not validate a prospective ≤3 cm protocol.
definitions: “Very early” in this paper means one iCCA ≤2 cm, not the current allocation-guidance definition.
icca-lt.uncertainty: Intervals for these estimates are not reported in the cited abstract.

pcca-itt.title: pCCA: transplant-protocol outcomes
pcca-itt.context: Neoadjuvant therapy with intent to transplant
pcca-itt.caution: Includes patients who never reached transplant. It is not a comparison with resection or contemporary systemic therapy.
pcca-itt.uncertainty: Five-year estimate 53% (95% CI 46–60). Figure 3A starts follow-up at presentation; the dropout analysis uses a different clock, the end of chemoradiation.

pcca-rfs.title: pCCA: recurrence-free after transplant
pcca-rfs.population: Protocol-treated pCCA recipients within the 12-center cohort
pcca-rfs.caution: A different endpoint and starting population from protocol-entry survival; do not compare the two percentages as treatment benefit.
pcca-rfs.uncertainty: Five-year recurrence-free survival 95% CI 57–73%. Survival analysis included 214 transplanted patients (Figure 3B).

pcca-nodes.title: pCCA: lymph nodes after resection
pcca-nodes.caution: Small observational cohort. These are resection outcomes, not evidence that nodal disease is acceptable for transplant.
definitions: Nodal staging describes regional versus distant nodes and current versus previously treated disease; these situations are not interchangeable.
pcca-nodes.uncertainty: Intervals for these estimates are not reported in the cited abstract.

net-grade.title: NET G3 versus NEC
net-grade.population: NORDIC NEC2; advanced digestive high-grade neoplasms receiving palliative chemotherapy
net-grade.caution: Prognostic association in treated advanced disease; not a transplant cohort. Verify morphology, not Ki-67 alone.
definitions: NET G3 and NEC both have high proliferation, but differ in differentiation. Ki-67 >20% is grade 3; a 55% split is not the diagnostic boundary between NET and NEC.
net-grade.uncertainty: Median OS: NET G3 21.8 months (95% CI 17.2–26.3); NEC 7.4 (6.3–8.4). First-line regimens differed; NET G3 often received temozolomide-based treatment, and platinum/etoposide had worse outcomes within NET G3. Two patients lacked calculable PFS/OS.

mixed-lt.title: Combined HCC–CCA versus HCC
mixed-lt.caution: Retrospective selected recipients; similar observed survival does not establish equivalence or routine candidacy. Recurrence was higher with combined HCC–CCA.
mixed-lt.uncertainty: Intervals for these estimates are not reported in the cited abstract.

hca-risk.title: Hepatic adenoma: observed complications
hca-risk.population: Multicenter molecular HCA cohort; 533 adenomas in 411 patients
hca-risk.caution: These are observed cohort frequencies, not annual or five-year risks. Selection and subtype matter.
definitions: β-catenin subtype needs mutation-level interpretation; exon 3 and exon 7/8 alterations should not be pooled as one risk category.
hca-risk.uncertainty: Intervals for these estimates are not reported in the cited abstract.

pdac-adjuvant.title: Resected PDAC: adjuvant outcomes
pdac-adjuvant.population: PRODIGE24; fit patients after R0/R1 PDAC resection
pdac-adjuvant.caution: Trial-selected postoperative patients; not a comparison of resectable versus unresectable disease.
pdac-adjuvant.uncertainty: OS HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.54–0.85). Median OS: 53.5 versus 35.5 months.

ipmn-risk.title: Branch-duct IPMN: long-term cancer risk
ipmn-risk.population: University of Tokyo branch-duct IPMN cohort, diagnosed 1994–2017
ipmn-risk.caution: Includes both IPMN-derived carcinoma and separate concomitant PDAC. This is not the probability that an individual cyst transforms.
ipmn-risk.uncertainty: Intervals for these estimates are not reported in the cited abstract.

amp-subtype.title: Ampullary carcinoma: histologic subtype
amp-subtype.population: Resected ampullary carcinoma, 1999–2016; 119 subtyped of 170 cases
amp-subtype.caution: Single-center association; stage and nodal involvement also differed. Subtype alone is not an individual survival prediction.
definitions: Pancreatobiliary 58%, intestinal 34.5%, mixed 7.6% in this cohort. Histologic phenotype is distinct from mutation status.
amp-subtype.uncertainty: Intervals for these estimates are not reported in the cited abstract.

pnet-small.title: Small nonfunctioning pNET: surveillance
pnet-small.population: ASPEN; asymptomatic sporadic nonfunctioning tumors ≤2 cm
pnet-small.caution: Interim, nonrandomized follow-up; zero observed events does not establish zero lifetime risk. Main-duct dilation, growth and patient factors still change management.
pnet-small.uncertainty: Intervals for these estimates are not reported in the cited abstract.

houston-hcc.title: Houston waiting outcomes
houston-hcc.population: HCC exception applicants; three pooled Houston programs; entrants 2021–2025
houston-hcc.caution: Historical aggregate; not an individual wait prediction.
definitions: Death / too-sick removal is a waitlist outcome, not cancer-specific mortality. Other removals and living donation compete with both displayed outcomes.
houston-hcc.uncertainty: 95% CI: transplant 35.8–45.7%; death/too sick 15.4–23.0%. Still at risk immediately before 12 months: 103.

houston-all.title: Houston waiting outcomes
houston-all.population: All adult first listings; three pooled Houston programs; entrants 2021–2025
houston-all.caution: Historical aggregate; not an individual wait prediction. All diagnoses: not a disease-specific estimate for this cancer.
definitions: Death / too-sick removal is a waitlist outcome, not cancer-specific mortality. Other removals and living donation compete with both displayed outcomes.
houston-all.uncertainty: 95% CI: transplant 47.4–51.2%; death/too sick 13.9–16.6%. Still at risk immediately before 12 months: 629.

net-lt.title: Milan-NET cohort: long-term outcomes
net-lt.population: Milan-NET-eligible liver metastases; nonrandom treatment allocation
net-lt.caution: Not randomized; transplant recipients were younger. Follow-up starts at primary resection, not transplant. These values do not establish a causal transplant benefit.
definitions: Milan-NET selection in this study: low-grade, portal-drained primary resected; ≤50% liver involvement; stable/responding disease for ≥6 months; age <60 a relative criterion.
net-lt.uncertainty: Five-year percentage confidence intervals are not reported in Table3. Left-truncated Cox analyses addressed delayed entry for transplanted patients.

ehs.title: Extrahepatic spread: observational cohort
ehs.population: Japanese advanced-HCC cohort, 2009–2014; Child-Pugh A/B and ECOG 0–1
ehs.caution: No significant survival difference in this historical treated cohort (P=0.765). This comparison does not change transplant selection criteria. No extrahepatic spread does not mean no vascular invasion.
definitions: Extrahepatic spread means tumor outside the liver, such as lung, bone, lymph nodes or peritoneum. Vascular tumor invasion is a separate finding.
ehs.uncertainty: Unadjusted observational comparison; treatment selection and liver reserve differ. Median follow-up 8.6 months. Modern immunotherapy outcomes cannot be inferred from these estimates.

hehe-score.title: HEHE recurrence risk after transplant
hehe-score.caution: Post-transplant recurrence-risk stratification; pathology-dependent and not a pretransplant eligibility calculator.
definitions: Add 5 points for pathological macrovascular invasion, 3 for waiting-list registration to LT ≤120 days, and 2 for pathological hilar lymph-node invasion.
Vascular and nodal pathology may only be confirmed at surgery; pre-LT imaging cannot automatically substitute.
hehe-score.uncertainty: Retrospective derivation cohort; high-score group only 17 patients. Table 6 does not report confidence intervals. The waiting-time association does not establish that deliberately delaying LT improves outcomes. Only 4 high-score recipients remained at risk at 60 months (Figure 2).

sharp-ehs.title: SHARP: extrahepatic spread, by trial arm
sharp-ehs.caution: Exploratory subgroups: no uniform survival penalty from extrahepatic spread across arms. No extrahepatic spread does not mean no vascular invasion.
definitions: EHS = extrahepatic spread; MVI = macroscopic vascular invasion. These are separate, overlapping findings.
sharp-ehs.uncertainty: Patients were randomized to treatment, not to EHS status. These historical subgroup estimates do not establish a treatment-by-EHS interaction or describe modern immunotherapy or transplant outcomes. Median-specific confidence intervals are not reported in the table.
